The general structure: Define a logical relation indexed by types where two terms are related if they are observationally equivalent at that type. Since we need noninterference with respect to erasure, and the labels are attached to types, the LR should express "any two computations related at type T produce equal erased values, and, moreover, if erasures of the values are equal then..." Something like a "term relation" that lets us swap between two runs at a secret type.

A standard approach for termination-insensitive noninterference proofs with logical relations: define relation `R_T(v1, v2)` on values (erased equality, plus structural conditions), and `E_T(t1, t2)` on terms: for any v1,v2, t1 ⇓ v1 -> t2 ⇓ v2 -> R_T(v1,v2). So the relation is a symmetric relation over pairs of terms of the same type, and noninterference follows because the "secret" parts don't influence the result whose indirect_reader doesn't read the secret's indirect_reader.

Wait but both t1 and t2 have type T_secret — that's not the usual two-level setting where we have "low-equivalent" inputs. Let's just build our own sound relation. We control both the relation and proof. The risk is proving the fundamental theorem where the rules force something impossible. Let's carefully choose the relation so that:
(A) Fundamental theorem for all typing rules, all observer levels ℓ.

Let me reconsider the design of V. A more semantic approach: rather than parameterizing by a single label, parameterize by a *security requirement* that says which observations must match. Inductive eval : tm -> tm -> Prop :=
| e_unit : forall k, eval (tm_unit k) (tm_unit k)
| e_abs : forall A body k, value (tm_abs A body k) -> eval (tm_abs A body k) (tm_abs A body k)
| e_pair : eval t1 v1 -> eval t2 v2 -> eval (tm_pair t1 t2 k) (tm_pair v1 v2 k)
| e_inl : eval t v -> eval (tm_inl t k) (tm_inl v k)
| e_inr : eval t v -> eval (tm_inr t k) (tm_inr v k)
| e_app : eval t1 (tm_abs A body k) -> eval t2 v2 -> flows_to k.reader r -> eval (tm_protect k.ind (open body v2)) v -> eval (tm_app t1 t2 r) v
| e_fst : eval t (tm_pair v1 v2 k) -> flows_to k.reader r -> eval (tm_protect k.ind v1) v -> eval (tm_fst t r) v
| e_snd : ... v2 ...
| e_case_l : eval t (tm_inl v k) -> flows_to k.reader r -> eval (tm_protect k.ind (open body1 v)) v' -> eval (tm_case t body1 body2 r) v'
| e_case_r : ...
| e_protect : eval t v -> eval (tm_protect l t) (protect_value v l)
| e_if_l : eval c (tm_inl v k) -> flows_to k.reader r -> eval (tm_protect k.ind yes) v' -> eval (tm_if c yes no r) v'
| e_if_r : ... no ...

And E ℓ T t1 t2 fits: E ℓ T t1 t2 := ∀ v1 v2, eval t1 v1 -> eval t2 v2 -> Vp ℓ T (security_of T) v1 v2.

This is structurally recursive! But Vp's visibility depends on the passed security κ, not on T's top security. The application's result type for a function whose *type annotation* is κ: T_App gives ty_protect κ.ind B — wait, the typing rule uses the arrow's security annotation from the type, which here is κ. However, one subtlety: Vp at type B with security κ_B: the sum clause's visibility uses κ_B. But when we call Vp ℓ B (protect_security (security_of B) k.ind), the components A1,A2 of B get their own securities. Good.

So Vp (with an explicit top-security parameter) is structurally recursive. But does it interact correctly with the "protection lemma"? V_ℓ (ty_protect l T) (protect v1 l)(protect v2 l) with V = Vp ℓ T (security_of T) and ty_protect l T has top security protect_security (security_of T) l, i.e., need Vp ℓ T (protect_security (security_of T) l) (protect v1 l)(protect v2 l) from Vp ℓ T (security_of T) v1 v2. This is now a lemma about Vp with changing security parameters, proved by induction on T (structural!). At each case: visibility: flows_to (protect κ l).ind ℓ ↔ flows_to κ.ind ℓ ∧ flows_to l ℓ. If target visible, source visible and l flows to ℓ. For sums: same constructor & payload Vp at A with security_of A (unchanged), plus the values' constructor annotations changed by protect—irrelevant. We get payload relation from source Vp; note source Vp uses the same security_of A. Good. For arrows: source Vp ℓ (Arrow A B k) κ v1 v2, target Vp ℓ (Arrow A B k) (protect κ l) (protect v1 l)(protect v2 l). Target's arrow clause: for all r args with Vp A (security_of A) args, eval (app (protect v1 l) a r) results → need Vp ℓ B (protect_security (security_of B) (protect κ l).ind) results. Source's clause gives eval (app v1 a r) → Vp ℓ B (protect_security (security_of B) κ.ind) results. As before, we need to transfer along evaluation equivalence between app (protect v1 l) and protect l (app v1 r), and then apply the protection lemma at type B with security κ_B = protect_security (security_of B) κ.ind and level l. That's an IH at B (structurally smaller) with the security parameter varying — exactly the induction hypothesis of the lemma (which quantifies over all security parameters). 

So with Vp structurally recursive, the key "protection lemma" can be proved by induction on T with a generalized security parameter and labels: 

Lemma Vp_protect : forall T ℓ κ v1 v2 l,
  Vp ℓ T κ v1 v2 ->
  Vp ℓ T (protect_security κ l) (protect_value v1 l) (protect_value v2 l).

Plus the evaluation-equivalence lemma and the term-level protection lemma E_protect.

Alternatively, define E as a Fixpoint mutually with Vp:

The guard checker for mutual fixpoints requires recursive calls on a structurally smaller argument of the same mutually-defined function? In mutual fixpoints, calls between the functions do not themselves need to be on smaller arguments as long as the whole call graph decreases; Coq's guard condition for mutual fixpoints requires each recursive call to be on a structurally smaller argument of the same function's principal argument, and cross-calls are allowed if the decreasing argument is the same? Here Vp calls E at ty_protect B and E calls Vp at the same T. E's call to Vp at the same T is not smaller → rejected likely. So inline E.

So:

```
Fixpoint Vp (ℓ : label) (T : ty) (κ : security) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => True
  | Ty_Sum A B _ =>
      if flows_to_dec κ.(indirect_reader) ℓ then
        (exists a1 a2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inl a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 k2 /\
           Vp ℓ A (security_of A) a1 a2)
        \/ (exists b1 b2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inr b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr b2 k2 /\
           Vp ℓ B (security_of B) b1 b2)
      else True
  | Ty_Prod A B _ =>
      if flows_to_dec κ.(indirect_reader) ℓ then
        (exists a1 b1 a2 b2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\
           Vp ℓ A (security_of A) a1 a2 /\ Vp ℓ B (security_of B) b1 b2)
      else True
  | Ty_Arrow A B _ =>
      if flows_to_dec κ.(indirect_reader) ℓ then
        forall (r : label) (t1 t2 : tm),
          (forall w1 w2, eval t1 w1 -> eval t2 w2 -> Vp ℓ A (security_of A) w1 w2) ->
          forall w1 w2, eval (tm_app v1 t1 r) w1 -> eval (tm_app v2 t2 r) w2 ->
            Vp ℓ B (protect_security (security_of B) κ.(indirect_reader)) w1 w2
      else True
  end.
```

So the Vp_protect lemma is provable by induction on T with IH at B. Let's write it carefully later.

Now, the subtyping monotonicity lemma. Statement:
Lemma subtype_sound : forall T U, subtype T U -> forall ℓ (v1 v2 : tm),
  Vp ℓ T (security_of T) v1 v2 -> Vp ℓ U (security_of U) v1 v2.
Prove by induction on the subtype derivation.
- S_Unit k1 k2: wf1 wf2 le. Vp at Unit = True; Vp at Unit = True. trivial.
- S_Sum T1 T2 U1 U2 k1 k2: IH1: Vp at T1 → Vp at U1 (with security_of). IH2 similarly. Need: Vp ℓ (Sum T1 T2 k1) k1 v1 v2 → Vp ℓ (Sum U1 U2 k2) k2 v1 v2.
  If target invisible (k2.ind ⋢ ℓ): target True. Done.
  If target visible (k2.ind ⊑ ℓ): need source visible to use hypothesis: le gives k1.ind ⊑ k2.ind, so k1.ind ⊑ ℓ. Source visible, so Vp source gives (inl case) v1 = inl a1 ka1, v2 = inl a2 ka2, Vp ℓ T1 (sec T1) a1 a2. Need target inl case with Vp ℓ U1 (sec U1) a1 a2: by IH1. Done.
- S_Prod similarly.
- S_Arrow T1 T2 U1 U2 k1 k2: premise subtype U1 T1 (contravariant), subtype T2 U2; wf; le k1 k2.
  IH_dom: Vp at U1 → Vp at T1 (i.e., for all values, Vp ℓ U1 (sec U1) → Vp ℓ T1 (sec T1)).
  IH_cod: Vp at T2 → Vp at U2.
  Need Vp ℓ (Arrow T1 T2 k1) k1 v1 v2 → Vp ℓ (Arrow U1 U2 k2) k2 v1 v2.
  If k2.ind ⋢ ℓ: target True.
  If k2.ind ⊑ ℓ: source visible: k1.ind ⊑ k2.ind ⊑ ℓ. Source clause: ∀ r t1 t2, E ℓ T1 t1 t2 → evals of app v1 t1 r → Vp ℓ T2 (protect (sec T2) k1.ind) w1 w2.
  Target clause: ∀ r t1 t2, E ℓ U1 t1 t2 → evals of app v1 t1 r → Vp ℓ U2 (protect (sec U2) k2.ind) w1 w2.
  Given E ℓ U1 t1 t2, need E ℓ T1 t1 t2: E means ∀ evals, Vp at T1 of results. From E U1 evals get Vp U1 at results; by IH_dom get Vp T1. So E T1 holds.
  Then source gives Vp ℓ T2 (protect (sec T2) k1.ind) w1 w2 for evals of the app.
  Need Vp ℓ U2 (protect (sec U2) k2.ind) w1 w2. This is the "protected subtype" monotonicity: T2 ≤ U2 and k1.ind ⊑ k2.ind. We need a lemma:
    subtype_protect_sound : subtype T2 U2 -> flows_to l1 l2? -> ... Vp ℓ T (protect_security (security_of T) l1) ⊆ Vp ℓ U (protect_security (security_of U) l2).
  Prove by induction on the subtype derivation? The structure of the statement: Vp at T with security κ1 → Vp at U with security κ2, given security_le-ish conditions between κ1 and κ2 (here κ1 = protect (sec T) k1.ind, κ2 = protect (sec U) k2.ind; note sec T ≤ sec U from S_Arrow's le, and k1 ≤... ). More generally, prove a monotonicity lemma parameterized by security κ_T ≤ κ_U:
  
  Lemma Vp_sub : forall T U, subtype T U -> forall ℓ κT κU v1 v2,
     security_le κT κU ->
     Vp ℓ T κT v1 v2 -> Vp ℓ U κU v1 v2.

  Can we prove this by induction on subtype? Let's check the cases with arbitrary κT, κU.
  - S_Unit: True.
  - S_Sum T1 T2 U1 U2 k1 k2 with component subtypes and le k1 k2. Claim for arbitrary κT ≤ κU. If κU.ind ⋢ ℓ: True. Else κT.ind ⊑ κU.ind ⊑ ℓ. Source visible. Source gives inl/inr with Vp ℓ T1 (sec T1). Need Vp ℓ U1 (sec U1) — by IH1 with κT = sec T1, κU = sec U1, requiring security_le (sec T1) (sec U1); from the subtype derivation S_Sum, the component subtyping doesn't directly give security_le of components! The S_Sum constructor has premises subtype T1 U1 which recursively may imply... Security_le of component types should be a consequence of subtype T1 U1 (a "security_of_subtype" lemma). Need to prove: subtype T U → security_le (security_of T) (security_of U). Is that true by induction on subtype? S_Trans: compose. S_Arrow: security_le k1 k2 is a premise → for arrow types security_of = k. S_Sum/Prod/Unit: premises include security_le k1 k2. So yes, prove `subtype_security_le`.
    Then IH1 needs security_le (sec T1) (sec U1): from subtype_security_le (subtype T1 U1). Good. Also the visibility for the recursive call: target Vp U1 with κU = sec U1; is it visible? We need? IH gives: if security_le (sec T1) (sec U1) and Vp T1 (sec T1) then Vp U1 (sec U1), no visibility conditions needed in the lemma statement. Good.
  - S_Prod similarly.
  - S_Arrow T1 T2 U1 U2 k1 k2 with subtypes U1 T1 and T2 U2, le k1 k2, arbitrary κT ≤ κU. Target visible: κU.ind ⊑ ℓ. Source visible: κT.ind ⊑ κU.ind ⊑ ℓ.     Need E ℓ T1 t1 t2 from E ℓ U1: by IH_dom with κT=sec U1, κU=sec T1: subtype U1 T1, security_le (sec U1)(sec T1) from subtype_security_le; applied pointwise in E. Good.
    Then source gives Vp ℓ T2 (protect (sec T2) κT.ind) w1 w2. Need Vp ℓ U2 (protect (sec U2) κU.ind) w1 w2. So need a lemma security_le_protect_compat. Then done.
  - S_Trans T U V: subtype T U, subtype U V, IH1, IH2; chain.
  
  Great: a single generalized monotonicity lemma `subtype_Vp` with arbitrary κT κU and security_le κT κU. And `subtype_security_le`.

  Note: the arrow clause in Vp with arbitrary κ uses κ.ind for protection of codomain and visibility; in the subtype case, κT and κU correspond to the top security of the types being compared. Good.

Let's now define Vp precisely with bounds.

Notation:
```
Definition sec_ind k := k.(indirect_reader).
Definition sec_rd k := k.(reader).
```

Vp ℓ T κ v1 v2:
```
match T with
| Ty_Unit _ =>
    if flows_to κ.ind ℓ then exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2 /\ security_le k1 κ /\ security_le k2 κ
    else True
| Ty_Sum A B _ =>
    if flows_to κ.ind ℓ then
      (exists a1 a2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inl a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 k2 /\ security_le k1 κ /\ security_le k2 κ /\ Vp ℓ A (security_of A) a1 a2)
      \/ (exists b1 b2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inr b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr b2 k2 /\ security_le k1 κ /\ security_le k2 κ /\ Vp ℓ B (security_of B) b1 b2)
    else True
| Ty_Prod A B _ =>
    if flows_to κ.ind ℓ then
      exists a1 b1 a2 b2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\ security_le k1 κ /\ security_le k2 κ /\ Vp ℓ A (sec A) a1 a2 /\ Vp ℓ B (sec B) b1 b2
    else True
| Ty_Arrow A B _ =>
    if flows_to κ.ind ℓ then
      exists k1 k2, ??? values are abs? 
      forall r t1 t2, E ℓ A t1 t2 -> forall w1 w2, eval (app v1 t1 r) w1 -> eval (app v2 t2 r) w2 -> Vp ℓ B (protect (sec B) κ.ind) w1 w2
    else True
end
```
For the arrow, to enforce the value annotation bound, we need to know the value's annotation. If v1 is an abs, we can extract via shape: require v1 = tm_abs A1 body1 k1 with security_le k1 κ? But what if v1 is not an abs? Typed values at arrow type are abs (by progress), but semantically the relation could allow non-abs values vacuously. For the invariant needed in T_App, the function value f comes from evaluating a typed term, so should be an abs with bounded annotation — but our E/arrow relation must guarantee it. If Vp arrow doesn't require abs shape, then in T_App the function value might be non-abs; then app is stuck on both sides? If one side's f is an abs and the other isn't, one app evaluates and the other doesn't → E vacuous. But the *fundamental theorem* expects E of the app terms, which is vacuous if one side stuck, so fine. But if both are abs with unbounded annotations, then the flow condition k_v.reader ⊑ r might fail and both stuck → fine. However, the result type protection uses k.ind, and the step uses k_v.ind; we need the bound to relate protection levels. If both sides stuck, no problem; if they evaluate, their annotations may be arbitrary... Could a typed term's value at arrow type be an abs with an annotation not ≤ the type's annotation? Let's see: T_Abs gives annotation = type's. T_Sub/T_Protect only raise. Env values: γ x with E at the arrow type; if Vp arrow doesn't enforce the bound, γ x could be an abs with annotation High while the type says Low; then the If/App proof's join bound fails. But wait, the env values in the fundamental theorem are arbitrary terms satisfying E; if the LR doesn't enforce bounds, the theorem might fail for such env values. But the theorem is about terms t1,t2 substituted for x; at the top level, env values are t1,t2 (closed typed). The env relation needed at x's type is E, which is about *evaluation results*. If E doesn't enforce annotation bounds, we can't prove the fundamental theorem for arbitrary env values. So Vp arrow should require: the values, if they are abs, have bounded annotations; and to make it usable, require v1,v2 are abs values with bounded annotations? If we require abs shape, then Vp arrow is only inhabited by abs values. Is that a problem? In T_Abs, yes abs. In T_Sub, the same value. In T_Protect, protect_value of an abs is an abs. So fine. Subtyping soundness: same value, bound transfers via security_le_trans. So define:

Vp ℓ (Arrow A B _) κ v1 v2 :=
  if flows_to κ.ind ℓ then
    exists (A1 : ty) (body1 : tm) (k1 : security) (A2 body2 k2),
      v1 = tm_abs A1 body1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_abs A2 body2 k2 /\
      security_le k1 κ /\ security_le k2 κ /\
      forall r t1 t2, (∀ w1 w2, eval t1 w1 -> eval t2 w2 -> Vp ℓ A (sec A) w1 w2) ->
          forall w1 w2, eval (app v1 t1 r) w1 -> eval (app v2 t2 r) w2 ->
             Vp ℓ B (protect (sec B) κ.ind) w1 w2
  else True.

Hmm, do we need the domain types A1 of the abs values to relate to A? The body typing ensures the value is well-typed, but the semantic relation can ignore A1. For soundness of the final theorem, no need. But for Vp_protect arrow case, the abs shape and bound are preserved. For Vp_sec_irrel arrow: same values; bounds security_le ki κ1 and ki κ2 both hold if κ1,κ2 comparable? In the sec_irrel lemma we assume both κ1.ind, κ2.ind flow to ℓ, not security_le between them. Lemma multi_eval : forall t v, multi t v -> value v -> eval t v.

Now, the Vp definition. Let me write it:

```coq
Definition sec_rd (k : security) : label := k.(reader).
Definition sec_ind (k : security) : label := k.(indirect_reader).

Fixpoint Vp (l : label) (T : ty) (kappa : security) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ =>
      if flows_to_dec kappa.(indirect_reader) l then
        exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2 /\
                     security_le k1 kappa /\ security_le k2 kappa
      else True
  | Ty_Sum A B _ =>
      if flows_to_dec kappa.(indirect_reader) l then
        (exists a1 a2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inl a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 k2 /\
             security_le k1 kappa /\ security_le k2 kappa /\
             Vp l A (security_of A) a1 a2)
        \/
        (exists b1 b2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inr b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr b2 k2 /\
             security_le k1 kappa /\ security_le k2 kappa /\
             Vp l B (security_of B) b1 b2)
      else True
  | Ty_Prod A B _ =>
      if flows_to_dec kappa.(indirect_reader) l then
        exists a1 b1 a2 b2 k1 k2,
          v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\
          security_le k1 kappa /\ security_le k2 kappa /\
          Vp l A (security_of A) a1 a2 /\ Vp l B (security_of B) b1 b2
      else True
  | Ty_Arrow A B _ =>
      if flows_to_dec kappa.(indirect_reader) l then
        exists (A1 : ty) (body1 : tm) (k1 : security) (A2 : ty) (body2 : tm) (k2 : security),
          v1 = tm_abs A1 body1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_abs A2 body2 k2 /\
          security_le k1 kappa /\ security_le k2 kappa /\
          forall (r : label) (t1 t2 : tm),
            (forall w1 w2, eval t1 w1 -> eval t2 w2 -> Vp l A (security_of A) w1 w2) ->
            forall w1 w2,
              eval (tm_app v1 t1 r) w1 -> eval (tm_app v2 t2 r) w2 ->
              Vp l B (protect_security (security_of B) kappa.(indirect_reader)) w1 w2
      else True
  end.
```

Now let's think about **`Vp` and the `if flows_to` implication style with Coq's `simpl`**. Since the leading binder is a Prop (flows_to κ.ind l), the match branch is a function type. `simpl (Vp l (Ty_Sum A B k) κ v1 v2)` should reduce the Fixpoint and the match, yielding `flows_to κ.ind l -> (exists ...) \/ (exists ...)`. However, in definitions, when we write `simpl in H` where H : Vp l T κ v1 v2 and T is a variable, simpl does nothing. In proofs we destruct T or use the induction's constructor case where T is concrete. Fine.

Fixpoint subst_env (γ : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => tm_bvar i
  | tm_fvar x => γ x
  | tm_unit k => tm_unit k
  | tm_abs T body k => tm_abs T (subst_env γ body) k
  | tm_app t1 t2 r => tm_app (subst_env γ t1) (subst_env γ t2) r
  ...
  | tm_if c y n r => tm_if (subst_env γ c) (subst_env γ y) (subst_env γ n) r
  end.
```

Fixpoint max_list (l : list nat) : nat :=

(* Auxiliary lemmas about security levels                        *)

Lemma flows_to_refl : forall l, flows_to l l.
Proof. intros []; simpl; auto. Qed.

Lemma flows_to_trans : forall l1 l2 l3,
  flows_to l1 l2 -> flows_to l2 l3 -> flows_to l1 l3.
Proof. intros [] [] [] H1 H2; simpl in *; auto. Qed.

Lemma flows_to_join_l : forall l1 l2 l,
  flows_to (join l1 l2) l <-> flows_to l1 l /\ flows_to l2 l.
Proof. intros [] [] []; simpl; tauto. Qed.

Lemma flows_to_join_r1 : forall l1 l2, flows_to l1 (join l1 l2).
Proof. intros []; destruct l2; simpl; auto. Qed.

Lemma flows_to_join_r2 : forall l1 l2, flows_to l2 (join l1 l2).
Proof. intros []; destruct l1; simpl; auto. Qed.

Lemma join_assoc : forall a b c, join (join a b) c = join a (join b c).
Proof. intros [] [] []; reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma join_idem : forall a, join a a = a.
Proof. intros []; reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma flows_to_join_both : forall a b c,
  flows_to a c -> flows_to b c -> flows_to (join a b) c.
Proof. intros a b c H1 H2; apply flows_to_join_l; auto. Qed.

Definition fvsC:
```coq
Fixpoint fvsC (C : program_context) : list atom :=
  match C with
  | C_Hole => []
  | C_Abs T C' k => fvsC C'
  | C_AppLeft C' t r => fvsC C' ++ fv t
  | C_AppRight t C' r => fv t ++ fvsC C'
  | C_PairLeft C' t k => fvsC C' ++ fv t
  | C_PairRight t C' k => fv t ++ fvsC C'
  | C_Fst C' r => fvsC C'
  | C_Snd C' r => fvsC C'
  | C_Inl C' k => fvsC C'
  | C_Inr C' k => fvsC C'
  | C_CaseScrutinee C' b1 b2 r => fvsC C' ++ fv b1 ++ fv b2
  | C_CaseLeft t0 C' b2 r => fv t0 ++ fvsC C' ++ fv b2
  | C_CaseRight t0 b1 C' r => fv t0 ++ fv b1 ++ fvsC C'
  | C_Protect l C' => fvsC C'
  | C_IfCondition C' y n r => fvsC C' ++ fv y ++ fv n
  | C_IfThen c C' n r => fv c ++ fvsC C' ++ fv n
  | C_IfElse c y C' r => fv c ++ fv y ++ fvsC C'
  end.

  (forall x, In x (fvsC C) -> g x = tm_fvar x) ->
  subst_env g (plug C u) = plug C (subst_env g u).

  - (* C_AppLeft *) f_equal.

    + apply subst_env_id. intros x Hx. apply H. simpl. apply in_app_iff; right; exact Hx.
  ...
```

Definition:
```coq
Fixpoint Vp (l : label) (T : ty) (kappa : security) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
        (exists k1 k2 : security,
           v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2 /\
           security_le k1 kappa /\ security_le k2 kappa)
  | Ty_Sum A B _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
        ((exists (a1 a2 : tm) (k1 k2 : security),
            v1 = tm_inl a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 k2 /\
            security_le k1 kappa /\ security_le k2 kappa /\
            Vp l A (security_of A) a1 a2)
         \/
         (exists (b1 b2 : tm) (k1 k2 : security),
            v1 = tm_inr b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr b2 k2 /\
            security_le k1 kappa /\ security_le k2 kappa /\
            Vp l B (security_of B) b1 b2))
  | Ty_Prod A B _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
        (exists (a1 b1 a2 b2 : tm) (k1 k2 : security),
            v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\
            security_le k1 kappa /\ security_le k2 kappa /\
            Vp l A (security_of A) a1 a2 /\
            Vp l B (security_of B) b1 b2)
  | Ty_Arrow A B _ =>
      flows_to kappa.(indirect_reader) l ->
        (exists (A1 : ty) (body1 : tm) (k1 : security)
                (A2 : ty) (body2 : tm) (k2 : security),
            v1 = tm_abs A1 body1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_abs A2 body2 k2 /\
            security_le k1 kappa /\ security_le k2 kappa /\

              (forall (u1 u2 : tm), eval t1 u1 -> eval t2 u2 ->
                 Vp l A (security_of A) u1 u2) ->
              forall (u1 u2 : tm),
                eval (tm_app v1 t1 r) u1 -> eval (tm_app v2 t2 r) u2 ->
                Vp l B (protect_security (security_of B) kappa.(indirect_reader)) u1 u2)
  end.
```

Definition env_rel (l : label) (Gamma : context) (g1 g2 : atom -> tm) : Prop :=
  forall x T, lookup_context x Gamma = Some T -> E l T (g1 x) (g2 x).

Definition env_upd (g : atom -> tm) (x : atom) (v : tm) : atom -> tm :=
  fun y => if Nat.eqb y x then v else g y.

Lemma env_upd_lc : forall g x v, env_lc g -> locally_closed v -> env_lc (env_upd g x v).

Qed.

```
This is 4×2 = 8 cases, but contradictions close quickly; and in the constructive cases the names are known (sa/sb). This is verbose but deterministic. Lemma case_branch_E :
  forall ell Gamma T1 T Tbody g1 g2 body (IHbody : forall x, ~In x L -> forall ell g1 g2, env_lc g1 -> env_lc g2 -> env_rel ell (update Gamma x T1) g1 g2 -> E ell T (subst_env g1 (open body (fvar x))) (subst_env g2 (open body (fvar x))))

Lemma case_branch_E : forall ell Gamma T1 Tbody L
  (g1 g2 : atom -> tm) (body : tm) (p1 p2 : tm) (k1 k2 : security)
  (kappa : security) (v1 v2 w1 w2 : tm),

     env_lc h1 -> env_lc h2 ->

     E ell' Tbody (subst_env h1 (open body (tm_fvar x)))
                  (subst_env h2 (open body (tm_fvar x)))) ->
  env_lc g1 -> env_lc g2 -> env_rel ell Gamma g1 g2 ->
  Vp ell T1 (security_of T1) p1 p2 ->

  v2 = protect_value w2 k2.(indirect_reader) ->
  Vp ell Tbody (protect_security (security_of Tbody) kappa.(indirect_reader)) v1 v2.

      rewrite (upd_neq g1 x p1 y Hyx), (upd_neq g2 x p2 y Hyx).

    - apply env_lc_upd; assumption.
    - apply upd_same. }
